evidence.quote: it may become warranted to increase the federal funds rate sooner or at a faster pace than participants had earlier anticipated
Some participants also noted that it could be appropriate to begin to reduce the size of the Federal Reserve's balance sheet relatively soon after beginning to raise the federal funds rate.
Participants remarked that inflation readings had been higher and were more persistent and widespread than previously anticipated.
Most agreed that risks to inflation were weighted to the upside.
Participants pointed to a number of signs that the U.S. labor market was very tight, including near-record rates of quits and job vacancies, as well as a notable pickup in wage growth.
Many participants judged that the appropriate pace of balance sheet runoff would likely be faster than it was during the previous normalization episode.

parsed.rationale: The minutes signal earlier and faster rate hikes, a faster taper, and balance sheet runoff closer to liftoff and faster than last cycle, driven by persistent, broadening inflation and a very tight labor market. Omicron-related downside risks to activity are noted but are outweighed by emphasis on upside inflation risks.
